svg.text: Carboxylic acid derivatives: reactivity follows leaving-group quality
Fischer esterification: the alcohol's O stays in the ester (C–O–R); the acid's OH leaves as water.
Saponification is irreversible: the acid formed is deprotonated to carboxylate, which no longer reacts.
Acid chloride + amine makes an amide plus HCl, so a second equivalent of amine is needed as a base.
Peptide (amide) bonds survive in water for years: hydrolysis is favorable but has a high activation energy.
A peptide bond forms by condensation: amine N attacks the carboxyl C and water is lost.
